Electrical study · thumbnails · 2026-10-26

The words on the thumbnails

The text on the 82 recent winners' thumbnails (the top 50 of the last 90 days and the top 50 of the last 12 months, in scope, English, 5:00+). 49 of them are in your lane. The other 33 are fire or money videos, shown at the bottom for reference. The words were read off each image by a helper and re-checked by the main session against all 82 images. The text types are readings. A second helper sorted the same text blind and agreed on 65 of 73 (40 of 43 in your lane); with its calls the order below barely moves.

What the text does

  1. Short. The typical thumbnail with text has 4 words. Most use 2 to 5.
  2. Commands and questions lead. Among your-lane videos, “STOP DOING THIS”, “This Needs To STOP!”, “START HERE!” and questions like “WHICH ONE KILLS YOU?” or “Why 120V?” typically get about twice the views of a plain topic label (“RUN ELECTRICAL TO A SHED”).
  3. Plain topic labels are the most common and the weakest. 15 of 49, typical 211K. They work for real teachers with a following (Smarter Sparky, The Wiring Guide) more than for new channels.
  4. Repeating the title or adding to it makes little difference. Text that repeats the title: 18 videos, typical 332K. Text that adds something new: 25, typical 289K.
  5. The very biggest have no text at all (hack channels: “99% of People Connect Wires WRONG”, 10.8M). The picture does the work: a red X and a green check over two wires.

Samples are small (2 to 15 videos per type), so treat the order as a direction, not a rule. Views here are raw views, not compared with each channel's typical video.

Your look 1: character + explainer board

Nobody in this niche pairs a presenter with a blue blueprint board the way your two examples do. The nearest are below: diagram-only thumbnails (30 labelled, typical 3.0M), and a few that put a person beside a drawn diagram. The Wiring Guide's “Live Neutral Ground EXPLAINED” (1.0M) is the closest real example. Sparky Steve's AI man beside panel diagrams got 17K and 2.6K. So the look is open, and it isn't proven here yet.

Your look 2: a person reacting or pointing at the problem

31 labelled, typical 1.8M. Several of these are AI personas, and they did well in the last 90 days: Bertha's Clean Home “NOBODY CLEANS THIS” 710K, Frederick 439K, Ray Dutton's Garage 406K, Ramón Delgado 375K. So a character pointing at the problem can work. The small persona channels in the census mostly used dark AI scenes with something burning.
